findings.quote: FY23 net income of $9.5B exceeded that year's operating income, which points to non-operating items in that year, and FY25 net income of $8.7B and diluted EPS of $8.14 are a cleaner read of recurring earnings.
findings.issue: The income table shows net income above operating income in FY24 ($6.6B vs $5.4B) and FY25 ($8.7B vs $8.5B) as well as FY23, so by the paragraph's own test FY25 also carries non-operating items. Singling out FY23 and calling FY25 'a cleaner read of recurring earnings' is a claim the surface contradicts.
findings.fix: Say that net income exceeded operating income in each of FY23, FY24 and FY25, so non-operating items lift every year's bottom line, and that the pack does not let us size them. Drop 'cleaner read of recurring earnings', or anchor recurring earnings to operating income instead.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: The decline coincides with heavy share repurchases rather than losses, since the company was profitable in each of those years.
findings.issue: This is a causal reading the pack does not establish, and the table argues against it. In FY24 equity fell from $28.6B to $19.6B while net income was $6.6B and repurchases were $5.8B. Earnings alone more than offset the buyback, so repurchases cannot account for the drop. Some other equity movement, not on the surface, drove most of it. 'Rather than losses' therefore points the reader to the wrong cause.
findings.fix: State the equity decline and the repurchase figures side by side. Say the repurchases explain only part of the FY24 drop and that the pack does not show the remainder. Do not assign a cause.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: A 15.8% FCF margin in FY25 funds both reinvestment and repurchases. Cash generation at that level is evidence of pricing power, but a single strong year does not yet establish durability.
findings.issue: Two claims are contradicted elsewhere in the report. First, FY25 repurchases of $7.6B exceeded FCF of $7.3B, which cashflowCommentary itself says, so FCF did not fund both reinvestment and repurchases. Second, incomeCommentary says gross margin is unavailable and 'we cannot separate pricing from mix', so FCF margin is not evidence of pricing power. The same over-reach shows in executiveSummary.thesis.body ('turned a recovering engine franchise into a cash compounder'), which rests on the single year this factor says does not establish durability.
findings.fix: Say that FY25 FCF covered capital expenditure but not the full repurchase program. Remove the pricing-power inference. In the thesis, replace 'cash compounder' with a claim the FY24 to FY25 FCF figures support.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged; the 'covered capital expenditure' slip is fixed under F-28.

findings.quote: Services leverage: growth in the installed fleet feeds MRO and spare-parts demand, which should keep the mix moving toward higher-margin revenue.
findings.issue: The pack has no installed-fleet data, no services or equipment mix, and no service margin. durability concedes this ('comes without the installed-base, backlog or segment data'). The point asserts both an unseen mechanism and an unseen mix shift. Similarly, sections.businessMoat.durability asserts that flight activity and defense budgets 'Both have supported results recently', a causal claim with no MD&A, transcript or press release behind it.
findings.fix: Restate the point as a hypothesis the pack cannot confirm, or drop it. In durability, keep the cyclical dependence (aftermarket on flight activity, defense on budgets) but delete 'Both have supported results recently'.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: We judge management by results instead: the operating margin and free cash flow trends in FY24 and FY25 show a team executing on both growth and conversion.
findings.issue: FY24 free cash flow fell to $3.7B from $4.3B in FY23 and FCF margin fell from 12.2% to 9.5%. The FY24 cash-flow trend therefore does not show execution on conversion. The sentence also attributes company results to management, a causal link the pack does not establish.
findings.fix: Limit the claim to what the table shows: operating margin rose in FY24 and FY25 and FCF conversion improved in FY25 after weakening in FY24. Say that without a proxy excerpt naming officers or MD&A we do not attribute these results to individuals.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: The Bull case at $430 needs no heroics on earnings; it needs the market to keep paying today's forward multiple for FY27E.
findings.issue: The stated mechanisms do not produce the scenario prices. Today's forward multiple on FY27E is ~31.8x, and at $9.82 that is the current $312.04, not $430. The Bull needs a much higher multiple on FY27E than today's. The Base driver says 'The multiple drifts down modestly', but $355 on FY27E EPS of $9.82 is above today's ~31.8x FY27E multiple, so it is not a contraction on that basis. The Bear's 'both of which have precedent for richly valued industrials' rests on no precedent in the pack, and 'de-rates toward the market' names a market multiple the pack does not carry.
findings.fix: Anchor each scenario in words to a multiple on the surface (36.8x trailing, 39.5x NTM, ~31.8x FY27E) and state which earnings base and direction apply, so the implied prices follow from the drivers. Remove the 'precedent' and 'toward the market' claims or ground them.
findings.note: Addressed: the prices follow from the drivers. Bull about a sixth above $9.82 at 39.5x gives $450; Base about 35.2x on $9.82 gives $346; Bear ~31.8x on $7.91 gives $252.

findings.quote: What would change our view: growth falling toward the consensus FY26E rate earlier than expected, or repurchases continuing beyond free cash flow while the current ratio weakens further, would move us to HOLD.
findings.issue: The Base case, weighted 50%, is 'growth slows to the +10% consensus rate'. Growth falling to the consensus FY26E rate is therefore the central expectation behind the BUY, not a downgrade trigger. Repurchases already exceed free cash flow in FY24 and FY25 and the current ratio has already slipped below one, so the second trigger is the status quo.
findings.fix: Name downgrade triggers outside the Base case, for example growth below the consensus FY26E rate, or FY27E EPS consensus falling away from $9.82. Frame the buyback trigger as a change from the current pattern.
findings.note: Addressed: the triggers check out. At the September 15 low of $307.05, BUY derives under either growth rate: E +11.8% and R 0.66x on the FY27E rate, E +11.3% and R 0.63x on the FY26E rate. Under both rates BUY derives from about $310.59 down. SELL derives from about $360 up (about $359.63 or $361.37), a little above the $354.39 late-August high.

findings.quote: We set a $330–$390 target range, below the $396.81 consensus target, because the bear case is real
findings.issue: The same claim, that our range sits below consensus because we weight the bear case, appears in four places. analystCommentary has the quoted text. multiplesCommentary has 'Our range sits below the consensus target because we weight the bear case more heavily than the street'. scenarioCommentary has 'we hold our target range below the consensus target'. finalRecommendation.body[1] has 'We sit below the consensus target because the bear case at $255 is a plausible outcome'. The 'bear case is real / a real scenario' phrasing is also a tic, and it echoes the house brief's wording.
findings.fix: Argue the gap to consensus once, in scenarioCommentary. In the other places, point to it in a few words or drop it.
findings.note: Addressed: the gap to consensus is stated once, at the end of scenarioCommentary, and it now names both causes.

findings.quote: Share repurchases were $5.8B in FY24 and $7.6B in FY25, above free cash flow in both years.
findings.issue: Three sections tell the 'repurchases ran ahead of free cash flow' story, and two of them restate the figures. cashflowCommentary has the quoted text. capitalAllocation has 'The company bought back $7.6B of stock in FY25, more than its free cash flow'. risks.idiosyncratic[3] has 'repurchases of $7.6B in FY25 exceeded free cash flow of $7.3B'. analystCommentary and finalRecommendation.body[1] and [2] retell it again. The small dividend is also made twice: cashflowCommentary 'the payout is a small claim on cash beside the buyback' and capitalAllocation 'Dividends are a small use of cash at a 0.60% yield'.
findings.fix: Make the buyback-versus-FCF argument once, in capitalAllocation, where the judgment belongs. Have cashflowCommentary state the figures without the verdict, and have the risk item point back in words. Keep the dividend remark in one section.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: Consensus FY26E EPS of $7.91 sits below FY25 diluted EPS of $8.14 on the figures as presented
findings.issue: The FY26E EPS 'dip' is told four times. It is in analystCommentary, in multiplesCommentary ('that dip in FY26E consensus EPS'), in growth.points[2] ('a rebound from the FY26E EPS dip') and in risks.idiosyncratic[1] ('consensus EPS of $7.91 sits below the FY25 level'). Only the first carries the 'on the figures as presented' hedge. That hedge is warranted: the comparison sets reported diluted EPS against a consensus mean, and incomeCommentary already notes non-operating items in reported net income. The later three treat the dip as an established earnings decline.
findings.fix: State the comparison once and carry the basis caveat with it: reported diluted EPS against a consensus mean, possibly not like for like. Elsewhere, refer back in words, and do not build a risk item on a dip the report itself qualifies.
findings.note: Addressed: the scenarios no longer call FY26 a dip year. multiplesCommentary carries the comparison once with its caveat and says 'we do not read it as an earnings decline', and executiveSummary.risks[1] now speaks of the FY26E-to-FY27E step.

findings.quote: Second-quarter momentum: Q2'26 revenue of $13.3B grew faster than FY25's full-year rate, so the business entered the second half with growth accelerating rather than slowing.
findings.issue: No growth point names the reading that cuts the other way. Points [0]-[4] are all bullish, and [1] frames the consensus deceleration only as a route to upside. Point [0] also draws 'accelerating' from one quarter set against a full-year average, with no Q1'26 or prior-quarter series on the page.
findings.fix: Add a counter-case sentence built on figures already on the page, for example that consensus FY26E growth of +10% sits well below the Q2'26 pace. Soften 'accelerating rather than slowing' to the comparison the page supports: Q2'26 growth of +21.1% against FY25's +18.5%.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: We see nothing in that disclosure that raises a governance concern.
findings.issue: The section restates the proxy's related-person review process almost line by line and then gives a one-line all-clear. It does not read the Fidelity relationship for the holder, for example what a five-percent holder also acting as plan recordkeeper means for independence. It also does not say that the truncated excerpt carries no board composition, independence or executive pay, which the brief requires when governance material is not captured. The 'all-clear' could be read as covering governance generally.
findings.fix: Cut the process restatement to one clause and say what the Fidelity arrangement means, or does not mean, for a holder. Add that the excerpt does not cover board independence or executive pay, so we make no claim about either.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: Under the 2026-03-12 proxy statement
findings.issue: ISO dates remain in prose: governance opens 'Under the 2026-03-12 proxy statement' and leadership says 'dated 2026-03-12'. The rubric asks for dates in prose form.
findings.fix: Write 'March 12, 2026'.
findings.note: Addressed: leadership and governance now write 'March 12, 2026'.

findings.quote: it stands at {- 0.98 -} on a trailing basis
findings.issue: Spans wrap levels, not signed changes: balanceCommentary 'it stands at {- 0.98 -} on a trailing basis' and, new in this rewrite, cashflowCommentary 'and then {+ 15.8% +}'. Spans are reserved for signed changes or explicit positives and negatives.
findings.fix: Remove both spans, or wrap the explicit judgment instead, for example '{- below one -}'.
findings.note: Addressed: the level spans are gone; balanceCommentary now wraps the judgment '{- below one -}'.

findings.quote: The thesis is that FY27E consensus is achievable and the market will keep paying for it.
findings.issue: The headline thesis does not match the mechanism behind the BUY. Today the market pays ~31.8x on FY27E EPS of $9.82, which is the current $312.04. If consensus arrives and the market 'keeps paying' that multiple, the shares do not move. The Base price of $355 needs a higher multiple on FY27E, which scenarioCommentary concedes: 'still above the multiple the market pays on FY27E now'. analystCommentary makes the same slip: 'That multiple holds only if the street's FY27E numbers arrive' implies holding the multiple is the upside. The upside in Base and Bull therefore comes from a re-rating on FY27E, and neither summary field says so. Separately, multiplesCommentary says '$9.82 is the earnings base our scenarios rest on', but the Bear rests on $7.91.
findings.fix: In the thesis and analystCommentary, say the BUY needs both FY27E delivery and the market paying more for FY27E earnings than it does today, settling near the trailing multiple as FY27E becomes the near-term base, which is what the Base driver argues. In multiplesCommentary, say the Bull and Base rest on $9.82 and the Bear on FY26E-level earnings.
findings.note: Addressed: the thesis and analystCommentary describe the Base as today's current-year multiple held on FY27E consensus earnings, which matches the $388 price.

findings.quote: The risks we weigh most are thin liquidity, with a trailing current ratio of 0.98, and a multiple that leaves little room for a growth miss.
findings.issue: The summary fields say the same thing twice. analystCommentary's closing sentence repeats executiveSummary.risks[0] ('a 36.8x trailing P/E leaves little room for a growth miss', with the same phrase) and risks[1] ('the trailing current ratio is below one'). The thesis counter-case makes the liquidity point a third time ('the balance sheet carries less liquidity than the earnings suggest'), before balanceCommentary and risks.idiosyncratic[0] and [2] argue both. finalRecommendation.body[1] ('our Bear price of $255 sits below the 52-week low') also retells the Bear driver ('the price breaks the $268.91 52-week low').
findings.fix: Cut the risk sentence from analystCommentary, or make it a few-word pointer to Risks, and leave the exec-summary risk list as the only summary statement. In finalRecommendation.body[1], use a figure the page renders, such as the reward/risk or the bear-case downside, rather than repeating the Bear-versus-low comparison.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: The operating margin gains from FY23 to FY25 are consistent with a growing high-margin service stream, though we lack the split to prove it.
findings.issue: The pack carries no service mix, service growth or service margin, and growth.points[3] concedes there is 'no installed-base, mix or service-margin data'. The words 'growing' and 'high-margin' therefore describe the service stream from outside the surface, even inside a hedge. This is the only factor rated 'Strong', yet it is the only one with no figure behind it. 'Cash generation', which the table does support, is rated Moderate, and durability says the available evidence does not show how long the advantage lasts. The strength grades run the opposite way to the evidence.
findings.fix: Drop 'growing' and 'high-margin'. Say the pack does not let us attribute the margin gains to services. Either rate the factor Moderate, or ground the Strong rating in something on the surface, for example the company description's pairing of engine sales with MRO and spare parts, and say what would confirm it.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: Defense & Propulsion Technologies spans engines, avionics, power systems and named component brands such as Avio Aero, Unison, Dowty Propellers and Colibrium Additive.
findings.issue: The company description is told three times. companyOverview describes both segments and lists the brands 'Avio Aero, Unison, Dowty Propellers and Colibrium Additive'. segments[0].body re-describes both segments in its 'Qualitatively, ...' paragraph ('turboprop engines, transmissions, propeller systems and sensors'). moatFactors[1] lists the same brands again. The moat factor's only judgment is 'That breadth ... diversifies the customer base', which no figure supports and which names no counter-case.
findings.fix: Keep the description in companyOverview. Limit segments[0].body to the source disagreement and the choice of the consolidated figure. Have moatFactors[1] say what breadth does for the moat without listing the brands again, and add the counter-case: with no segment revenue, the defense share cannot be sized, so the diversification cannot be either.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: which ties revenue to the fleet already in service rather than to new deliveries alone
findings.issue: The rewrite of moatFactors[0] adds a claim that two other places already make. Aftermarket revenue tracks the engines in service, said three times in different words: moatFactors[0] ('ties revenue to the fleet already in service rather than to new deliveries alone'), growth.points[3] ('aftermarket revenue tracks the engines already flying, so a larger fleet could lift it') and durability ('aftermarket demand follows flight activity'). The rubric treats a paraphrase in two places as repetition. systemic already points back correctly ('named under the moat').
findings.fix: Make the fleet-in-service claim once, in moatFactors[0], where the moat argument sits. Have growth.points[3] point back in words, for example 'the aftermarket tie noted under the moat could lift revenue as the fleet grows; the pack carries no installed-base data', and have durability use the cycle point without restating the mechanism.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: Our Bull and Base cases rest on FY27E EPS of $9.82, and our Bear case on FY26E-level earnings.
findings.issue: The Bull driver rests on FY27E EPS 'comfortably above the $9.82 consensus'. $430 at about 39.5x implies roughly $10.90. So the Bull does not rest on $9.82. The F-15 fix text suggested this wording and caused the slip.
findings.fix: Say the Base rests on FY27E EPS of $9.82, the Bull on FY27E earnings above it, and the Bear on FY26E-level earnings.
findings.note: Addressed: the Bull now prices FY27E earnings above $9.82, and risks.idiosyncratic[1] and catalysts[1] name only the Base as resting on $9.82.

findings.quote: the FY27E recovery slips
findings.issue: Calling FY27E a 'recovery' assumes FY26E earnings fall below FY25. multiplesCommentary qualifies that comparison as possibly not like for like (consensus mean against reported diluted EPS, see F-10). The Bear driver ('the FY27E recovery slips') and scenarioCommentary ('needs the FY27E recovery to slip; neither step requires a collapse') treat the dip as established. In scenarioCommentary, 'neither step' also has only one step to refer to.
findings.fix: Use 'the FY27E earnings step', as growth.points[2] does, in place of 'recovery'. Rewrite the scenarioCommentary clause so 'neither step' has two antecedents, or drop it.
findings.note: Addressed: unchanged and still correct.

findings.quote: The cyclical exposures named under the moat, air travel for the aftermarket and government budgets for defense, are the main macro risks here.
findings.issue: The F-19 edit removed the aftermarket-to-flight-activity link from durability, which now reads only 'the cycle in commercial aviation and in government defense budgets'. systemic still points back to the moat for 'air travel for the aftermarket', a pairing the moat no longer states in those terms. The parenthetical now restates the exposures instead of pointing to them, and the pointer is slightly stale.
findings.fix: Shorten systemic's opening to a plain pointer, for example 'The aviation and defense-budget cycles named under the moat are the main macro risks here', and drop the parenthetical pairing.
findings.note: Addressed: systemic now reads 'The aviation and defense-budget cycles named under the moat'.

findings.quote: For the compression: once earnings grow again after the FY26E dip, the multiple on current-year earnings has less reason to stay above the trailing one.
findings.issue: The Base mixes earnings bases, and that choice decides the label. multiplesCommentary names today's current-year multiple (39.5x, the price over FY26E consensus of $7.91) as 'the like-for-like reference'. It also warns that the FY26E-vs-FY25 comparison 'may not be like for like', because reported diluted EPS carries non-operating items. The 36.8x trailing P/E is the price over reported trailing earnings, the basis that carries those items. The 39.5x and ~31.8x multiples are the price over consensus means. The Base is the only scenario that takes its multiple from one basis and applies it to another ($9.82 consensus). Its only argument for stepping down 2.7 turns is the FY26E dip, and the report says that dip may be a basis effect. If part of the gap between 36.8x and 39.5x is basis, the step-down lowers the Base mechanically rather than on evidence. Holding 39.5x gives a Base of about $388 and derives BUY (E about +13%). The driver honestly says the anchor decides the label, but that argument has to rest on one reference.
findings.fix: Argue the Base multiple on the reference the report names. Either keep a step-down from 39.5x and argue its size from page evidence on both sides that does not depend on the qualified dip. Or state that 36.8x is a reported-earnings trailing multiple applied to a consensus figure, say the gap to 39.5x may be partly a basis difference, and explain why 36.8x is still the level you believe. If neither holds, re-anchor the Base and let the derived label stand on whichever side of the BUY line it falls. Do not choose the multiple for the label it produces.
findings.note: Addressed for the basis point: multiplesCommentary says 'We use the consensus basis throughout', and every scenario applies a consensus-basis multiple to consensus EPS. The new anchor, 39.5x held a year out, raises a different question, taken up in F-29.

findings.quote: earnings a year out stay near the $7.91 FY26E consensus, and the market pays the ~31.8x it now pays on FY27E earnings, since without the step it has no reason to pay up for a dip year.
findings.issue: The Bear's story and its multiple do not match. The story is that the step 'slips by a year', so it is delayed, not lost. On the report's own reference, a delay recreates today's setup a year later: a dip-level current year with the step a year ahead. Today the market prices that setup at 39.5x, which is about today's price. The ~31.8x is taken from a different quantity (today's price over FY27E EPS). Against the reference it is a de-rate of about a fifth, and the driver neither states nor sizes that de-rate. 'No reason to pay up for a dip year' contradicts what the market is paying today for the same setup, unless the slip also costs the market's confidence, which the driver does not argue. The closing clause also reads backwards: after 'We go no lower', 'the past year's low shows the market has paid less recently' sits beside a Bear price of $252 that is below the $268.91 low. The market has not paid that little in the past year.
findings.fix: Say what a one-year slip does to the market's confidence in the step, and argue the de-rate from the 39.5x reference in words on page evidence, so the ~31.8x follows from the story rather than being borrowed from the FY27E column. Keep the 15% floor in view: a Bear that is only a delay at an unchanged multiple would not be a real downside, so the de-rate needs its own reason. Rewrite or drop the closing clause so it says what the 52-week low actually shows.
findings.note: Addressed: the Bear now argues lost confidence, not just delay, and states the de-rate as 'about a fifth below the reference'. The closing clause now says correctly that the market has not paid below $268.91 in the past year.

findings.quote: For more Bear weight, consensus FY26E EPS sits below FY25 diluted EPS, so on the consensus basis earnings have not tracked revenue, and the shares trade well below their 52-week high with no source in front of us explaining the fall. We judge the two evenly matched.
findings.issue: Neither reason for the Bear weight bears on the Bear story, which is that the FY27E earnings step slips. The FY26E dip sits inside all three scenarios, so it cannot favor one of them, and the report itself says the comparison may not be like for like. The unexplained price fall concerns the entry point, which the next paragraph covers and where it is told a second time. The Bull-side reasons, by contrast (Q2'26 growth well ahead of consensus, three years of operating-margin gains), speak directly against a slip. 'Evenly matched' is therefore asserted, not argued, yet this split decides the label: moving about three points of weight from Bear to Bull derives BUY (two points falls just short). A Bear weight must be argued on the Bear case itself.
findings.fix: Argue the 25% from what the page says about whether the FY27E step arrives, on both sides. For example, the sources in front of us carry no guidance, MD&A, backlog or call, so the step rests on consensus alone, against a Q2'26 pace and margin record that support it. Drop the price fall from the weighting argument, or say how it bears on the step. If the case for 25% holds, keep HOLD and keep saying the call is close. If it does not, change the weights and let the derived label follow.
findings.note: Addressed: the Bear weight is now argued on whether the FY27E step arrives, from both sides. The split also no longer decides the label: moving 20 points from Base to Bear (45% Bear) still derives BUY, as does 10 points from Bull to Bear. The deciding input is the Base multiple (F-29).

findings.quote: For it: Q2'26 revenue growth ran well ahead of the FY26E path, and the Street targets cluster near this level.
findings.issue: The Bull's own evidence points higher than its price. Revenue running ahead of consensus argues for earnings above consensus, yet the Bull holds FY27E EPS at $9.82 and the multiple at today's level. It is a no-change case with no upside driver of its own, while the Bear stacks an earnings slip on a de-rate. The previous draft's Bull priced above-consensus earnings; F-20 asked only that the wording match the price, not that the Bull be capped at consensus. Separately, scenarioCommentary says 'the gap is the Base multiple'. But the Bull itself, at $388, sits below the $396.81 consensus and $400.00 median targets, and so would a Base held at 39.5x. Part of the gap to the Street is therefore the choice to hold every scenario at consensus earnings. A Bull capped below where its own evidence points is a one-sided anchor, as much as an inflated one would be.
findings.fix: Either price what the Bull's evidence argues (FY27E earnings above the $9.82 consensus, described in words, at a stated multiple and argued from both sides), or keep $388 and say why the Bull stops at consensus earnings and that no scenario prices an above-consensus outcome. Correct 'the gap is the Base multiple' so it names both sources of the gap. Let the derived label follow.
findings.note: Addressed: the Bull now prices above-consensus earnings and is anchored to the $450.00 Street high. The 'a sixth' is what that target implies rather than what the evidence sizes, and the driver's own counter concedes as much. At 20% weight the Bull does not decide the label (a $420 Bull still derives BUY).

findings.quote: every Street target sits above the price
findings.issue: The valuation section makes several claims more than once. The Street-target point appears three times: multiplesCommentary 'Even the lowest target sits above the price', the Base driver 'Against it: every Street target sits above the price', and scenarioCommentary 'every Street target sits above the price'. scenarioCommentary re-argues the drivers' evidence: 'Q2'26 revenue growth ran well ahead of consensus' (the Bull driver has 'ran well ahead of the FY26E path', as do growth.points[0] and [1]) and 'operating margin rose for three straight years' (the Base driver has 'margins are still rising'). The unexplained price fall appears twice within scenarioCommentary itself: 'trade well below their 52-week high with no source in front of us explaining the fall' and 'The shares slid steadily from late August to the report date, and no source in front of us explains the move.' The Base mechanism is described in analystCommentary, the thesis, the third paragraph of multiplesCommentary, the Base driver and finalRecommendation.body[0] ('because we expect the multiple on earnings to narrow as FY27E becomes the current year').
findings.fix: Give each piece of evidence one home. The drivers carry each scenario's case for and against. scenarioCommentary argues only the weights and the entry point, and refers back to the drivers in words. State the Street-target fact once, in multiplesCommentary. Tell the price fall once, in the entry-point paragraph. Argue the Base mechanism in the Base driver and let the summary fields point to it.
findings.note: Addressed: the Street-target and price-fall points each appear once, scenarioCommentary refers back to the Bull driver for its evidence, and the summary fields point to Valuation.

findings.quote: FY25 free cash flow covered capital expenditure but not the full repurchase program.
findings.issue: Free cash flow is operating cash flow after capital expenditure, so it cannot 'cover' capex. The F-3 fix text suggested this wording, and that was the reviewer's slip. The point that stands is that FY25 free cash flow fell short of the $7.6B repurchase program, which capitalAllocation already makes.
findings.fix: Write 'FY25 free cash flow, after capital expenditure, fell short of the full repurchase program', or drop the sentence and point to capitalAllocation.
findings.note: Addressed: moatFactors[2] now reads 'FY25 free cash flow, after capital expenditure, fell short of the full repurchase program'.

findings.quote: For holding it: the market paid that price within the past year, and the consensus and median targets sit a little higher still. Against it: what follows FY27E is not on our page, and with margins paused the market may pay less for current-year earnings a year out. No page figure sizes that narrowing, so we hold the reference; this anchor decides the label.
findings.issue: Rolling today's 39.5x current-year multiple onto FY27E is today's price plus one year of consensus EPS growth: the Base's $388 is the price times $9.82 over $7.91. That anchor is allowed only if the report argues why the multiple holds a year out, from both sides. Here it does not. (1) The report's own Bear says 'today's multiple pays ahead for a step that rests on consensus alone' and puts the no-pay-ahead multiple about a fifth lower, at ~31.8x. Holding 39.5x a year out therefore assumes the market pays ahead again for a step beyond FY27E, which the Base's own counter says 'is not on our page'. (2) 'the market paid that price within the past year' is about a price, not a multiple. The 52-week high was paid on earlier expectations, and the shares have since fallen with no explanation in front of us. (3) 'No page figure sizes that narrowing, so we hold the reference' treats a risk it cannot size as zero. That is a default, not an argument. The mirror defect was flagged on the HOLD in F-23. The one independent support is the $396.81 consensus and $400.00 median Street targets.
findings.fix: Argue the Base multiple a year out on page evidence from both sides, and reconcile it with the Bear's pay-ahead logic. Either say why the market would still pay ahead once FY27E is the current year, for example by leaning explicitly on the Street targets as the independent check and saying what they assume, or let the Base give up part of the premium and say how much. Drop 'the market paid that price within the past year' as support, and replace the 'no page figure sizes that narrowing' default with a reasoned view. For balance, the scenarioCommentary math shows BUY survives a Base down to about 35.2x, a little over half the way from 39.5x to the ~31.8x no-pay-ahead level. A reasoned partial narrowing may keep BUY. Let the derived label follow whatever multiple the argument supports.
findings.note: Addressed: the Base no longer holds 39.5x by default. It gives up part of the premium through a stated mechanism that is reconciled with the Bear's pay-ahead logic, and the 52-week-high argument is gone. The new question is whether the one choice inside that mechanism, the one that decides the label, is argued. See F-32.

findings.quote: On these scenarios every close from the second week of September derives BUY, the earlier closes from late August derive HOLD, and a price at the 52-week high would derive SELL.
findings.issue: The September 8 close of $334.91 falls in the second week of September and derives HOLD (E about +9.4%, R about 0.38x). BUY starts with the September 9 close of $325.42. 'The earlier closes from late August' also leaves out the early-September closes (September 1 to 8), which derive HOLD too.
findings.fix: Write that every close from September 9 derives BUY, and that the closes from late August through September 8 derive HOLD.
findings.note: Addressed: the entry-point paragraph now says that only the October 2 close and the mid-September low derive BUY. That checks out: the September 30 and October 1 closes derive HOLD by a few hundredths of a point.

findings.quote: The rating holds as long as the market keeps paying today's current-year multiple on consensus earnings, the judgment argued under Valuation.
findings.issue: The sentence overstates how fragile the label is. scenarioCommentary states correctly that BUY holds until the Base multiple falls a little more than a tenth below the reference (to about 35.2x). The rating therefore does not need the market to keep paying the full 39.5x.
findings.fix: Align this with scenarioCommentary: the rating holds unless the multiple on FY27E consensus earnings a year out narrows by more than about a tenth from today's current-year multiple.
findings.note: Addressed: finalRecommendation.body[0] now says the rating holds only if the multiple narrows by no more than a little over a tenth, which matches the Base and scenarioCommentary.

findings.quote: but at the consensus revenue pace into FY27E rather than today's far larger earnings step: about a tenth above the no-pay-ahead multiple of our Bear case, a little over a tenth below the reference, near the lowest Street target.
findings.issue: The mechanism is real and grounded on the page. Today's premium (39.5x over ~31.8x) equals the FY26E-to-FY27E EPS step. The Base keeps one year of growth at the consensus FY27E revenue pace ($50.3B to $55.8B, about +11%), so ~31.8x times that gives about 35.2x and $346. That is not an arbitrary number. But it lands $0.40 above the BUY line (E +10.02%), and the label turns on the one choice the driver does not argue: which growth rate stands in for the year beyond FY27E. The page's other consensus rate, FY26E revenue at +10%, gives about 35.0x, a Base near $343, E about +9.5% and HOLD. The two rates are 0.9 points apart, which is well inside the method's own precision, and the coordinator has disclosed that the 35.2x threshold reached the author before the rewrite. On the page as written, the deciding choice cannot be told apart from a tuned one. The driver also never says why the revenue pace stands in for earnings growth (earnings tracking revenue once margins pause). A reader cannot check the arithmetic from the driver.
findings.fix: In the Base driver, state the mechanism in words: the no-pay-ahead multiple raised by one year of expected growth, with earnings tracking revenue because margins have paused. Then argue from page evidence why the FY27E revenue pace, and not the +10% FY26E rate or the Q2'26 pace, is the right stand-in for growth a year out. Say plainly that the FY26E rate would derive HOLD. Let the label land wherever the rate you can argue puts it. If the evidence cannot separate the two rates, say so: the label then sits inside the method's own error, and the report should either let the derived label stand and say it is a coin-flip, or, if it takes a more conservative label, state that it is a one-notch-conservative call and why. Do not adjust the multiple, weights or prices to move E across the line.
findings.note: Addressed: the Base driver states the mechanism and why revenue pace stands in for earnings growth (margins paused). It argues for the FY27E rate as the nearer one, says the FY26E rate would derive HOLD, and scenarioCommentary concedes the call sits inside the method's error. The multiple, weights and prices are unchanged. The published HOLD is stated as one notch more conservative than the derived BUY, with a reason, in the subtitle, analystCommentary, thesis, scenarioCommentary and finalRecommendation.body[0], and the five agree. The house rule is met.
